kinds.note: The four labels this module gives to a statement that is called a conservation statement. Assigning a label to a statement is the author's judgement; the criterion is written next to each.
kinds.by_construction: true whatever the records say, by arithmetic or by how its sides are derived (often both sides are computed from the same records), so the statement tells nothing about the system
kinds.auditable: the records could have made the statement false, often because its two sides were written separately
kinds.not_recorded: one of the quantities was never written down, so the statement can be neither confirmed nor refuted from the records
kinds.analogy: the statement borrows the vocabulary of a law without the conditions under which the law holds

what_noether_s_theorem_needs.note: What Noether's first theorem needs before it yields a conserved quantity, and the author's reading of whether PSY-001's use meets each condition. The reading is a judgement about a text, not a measurement.

conditions.condition: an action: one function of the system's whole history whose stationary points are the system's actual motions
conditions.reason: no action and no equations of motion are written for governance cycles

conditions.condition: a continuous symmetry: a family of transformations indexed by a real number that leaves the action unchanged
conditions.reason: the symmetry named is the sameness of one operation at a short list of named levels, which is a discrete correspondence

conditions.condition: the conserved quantity is derived from the action and the symmetry, not chosen
conditions.reason: p_L is defined by a formula, and the text allows it to stay constant or grow, which a conserved quantity cannot do

synthetic_controls.kind: synthetic: eight imaginary events; nothing here is measured in the repository
synthetic_controls.note: Hand-written cases with eight imaginary events, e1 to e8, in the encoding of observed-input.json. Commits 1 to 8 create the events, commit 9 exists only where a deletion is recorded, commit 10 moves events to the archive. The cases model a system in which the listing is counted separately from the log (shelves and a scan log), which is what makes an unrecorded loss or copy possible; in Git the listing is the last snapshot of the log. In four of the five cases a departure or an error is planted; expected_by_hand is what the audit must return and was written before the analysis ran.

clean.description: Nothing leaves: six events archived, two pending, and the listing agrees.
clean.reading: nothing left: every file created is listed where the history puts it

recorded_removal.description: Commit 9 deletes e2 from the pending folder. The deletion is in the history.
recorded_removal.reading: files left, and every departure is on record

silent_loss.description: The history is that of the clean case, but e2 is not in the archive listing and no record says why.
silent_loss.reading: the records do not explain the listing

duplicate.description: The history is that of the clean case, but e7 was copied into the archive listing while it is still pending.
duplicate.reading: the records do not explain the listing

offsetting_errors.description: Both errors at once: e2 is missing from the archive listing and e7 was copied into it.
offsetting_errors.reading: offsetting errors: the counts balance and the items do not

negative_controls.note: Each control changes a copy of the observed snapshot in one place; the observed results are untouched.
